root.label: Atomics and Memory Ordering

children.note: Inserting an unnamed : 0 bit-field separates neighboring fields into distinct locations.

children.note: Unordered conflicting accesses with one non-atomic write invalidate the whole program.

children.label: Happens-Before Relations
children.note: Mathematical ordering edges proving when one thread observes another's writes.

children.label: Sequenced-Before Order
children.note: Intra-thread evaluation ordering established within a single execution stream.

children.label: Synchronizes-With Edge
children.note: Inter-thread link created when an acquire load reads a release store.

children.label: Release Sequences
children.note: Chained atomic RMW operations preserve synchronization back to the initial release store.

children.label: Memory Order Spectrum
children.note: Six ordering tags balancing barrier cost against cross-thread guarantees.

children.label: Relaxed Counters
children.note: Guarantees indivisible operations and modification order without ordering nearby memory.

children.label: Acquire-Release Pairwise
children.note: Prevents earlier writes sinking past release and later reads hoisting above acquire.

children.label: Seq-Cst Global Total Order
children.note: Enforces one consistent global order S across all seq_cst atomic operations.

children.note: Why hardware store buffers break naive intuition without fences.

children.note: Acquire-release allows both cores to read zero because store buffers delay writes.

children.note: Verify is_always_lock_free so large structs do not silently fall back to hidden mutexes.

children.note: Idiomatic lock-free algorithms built from compare-exchange and standalone barriers.

children.note: Prefer compare_exchange_weak inside retry loops to avoid redundant LL/SC checks.

children.note: Release and acquire fences synchronize relaxed atomics only on the fast exit path.
